requirement: Make every Playwright test fail when the page logs a console error or throws an uncaught exception, with an ignore list for known noise and without masking the test's own failure.
skeleton: A ConsoleErrorCollector context manager holding ignore patterns and errors, with an ignore check, console and pageerror handlers, enter registering them, and exit removing them and asserting.
caption: A context manager for Playwright tests, written in the standard library against a duck-typed page with on and remove_listener methods and no third-party imports, that fails the block when the browser logs errors. ConsoleErrorCollector(page, *, ignore=()) keeps substring patterns to ignore and a list of errors. Its console handler records a message's text only when its type is error and no pattern occurs in it; its pageerror handler records the string form of an uncaught error unless ignored. Entering registers both handlers with page.on for console and pageerror. Exiting removes both with page.remove_listener and, only when the block raised nothing, raises AssertionError listing the errors joined by semicolons, so a real test failure is not masked. The fixture asserts a clean run detaching listeners, failing on console errors but not warnings, page errors, substring ignores, no collection after exit, and an unmasked original exception.

plan.intent: Catch silent frontend errors in end-to-end tests
constraints: Only console messages of type error are collected
Both listeners are removed on exit
AssertionError is raised only when the block itself succeeded

rationale.teaches: Register console and pageerror listeners on enter, always remove both on exit, filter by type and substring, and assert only when exc_type is None.
rationale.why: Leaked listeners keep collecting into finished tests, asserting over an in-flight exception replaces the real failure with a noisy one, and exact-match ignores never match real log lines.

ops.docstring: Fail a Playwright test on browser console errors and uncaught page errors.

candidates.why_wrong: Console warnings are treated as errors and fail clean pages.
The console listener stays attached after the block and keeps collecting.
An AssertionError about console errors replaces the test's real exception.
Ignore patterns must match the whole text, so known noise still fails.
Uncaught page exceptions are never observed and the test passes.
